# Model ensembles

Advice is increasingly based on an ensemble of assessment models that span structural uncertainty (natural
mortality, steepness, growth, data weighting). `ss3_ensemble()` combines the MVLN draws of several SS3 runs, as
`ss3diags::SSdeltaMVLN(weight = )` with `SSplotEnsemble(joint = TRUE)`: each model contributes draws in proportion
to its weight, and the joint ensemble pools them. Ratios to the targets are computed within each model, with its
own reference points, before pooling. `ss3plot_ensemble()` shows the models in colour and the joint ensemble in
black, with `ss3plot_trj()`.

The example uses the shortfin mako reference run and two retrospective peels as stand-ins for alternative models:

```{r ens, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 9}
ens <- ss3_ensemble(list(ref = retro.sma$replist1, alt1 = retro.sma$replist2, alt2 = retro.sma$replist3),
                    weights = c(0.5, 0.25, 0.25), iters = 1000)
attr(ens, "weights")
ss3plot_ensemble(ens)
```

The joint ensemble on its own, and its Kobe plot:

```{r ens-joint, fig.height = 3.5, fig.width = 8}
ss3plot_ensemble(ens, models = FALSE, type = c("B/Btgt", "F/Ftgt"))
```

```{r ens-kobe, fig.height = 4.5, fig.width = 6}
ss3plot_kobe(ens$Joint)
```

> **Weights and years.** Weights are normalised to sum to one; model $i$ contributes `round(iters * n * w_i)`
> draws. The joint ensemble covers the years common to all models. Models built from `FLStockR` with iterations
> (`ss3stk(output = "iters")`) are resampled to their number of draws.
